step1_analysis.description: A simple sub-circuit consisting of two NMOS transistors. One is always on (gate tied to VDD) acting as a constant current draw or dummy load, and the other is driven by an input/bias voltage, acting as a variable current sink. This is likely a fragment of a larger digitally controlled delay element.

paper_reference.title: A Monotonic Digitally Controlled Delay Element

static_power.description: Total static power consumption of the circuit at nominal bias.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The extracted circuit has large W/L ratios (10) and one transistor is fully on (Vgs=1.8V), leading to higher power consumption in SKY130 at 1.8V compared to the full delay element reported in the paper (which likely operates with smaller bias currents or duty cycles).

total_current.description: Total DC current drawn from the VDD supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: Sum of currents through XM1 and XM2: 2.57 mA + 0.31 mA = 2.88 mA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using standard square-law saturation equations for SKY130 NMOS parameters.

transconductance_gm.description: Transconductance of the input-driven transistor (XM2) with respect to LABEL_NET_0.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Derived from the derivative of the drain current with respect to the gate voltage at the nominal 0.9V bias point.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the static operating point (current and power) and perform a DC sweep to extract the transconductance of the input transistor.
step3_testbench.spice:
* NMOS Bias/Load Circuit Testbench

.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

* DUT
XM2 VDD LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM1 VDD VDD GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
* 1. Operating Point Analysis
op
let total_current = -i(VVDD)
let total_pwr = total_current * 1.8
print total_current
print total_pwr

* 2. DC Sweep for Transconductance
dc VLABEL_NET_0 0 1.8 0.01
let gm_total = deriv(-i(VVDD))
meas dc gm_at_09 find gm_total at=0.9
meas dc gm_max max gm_total

quit
.endc
